editorial:
Imagine being so broke that you would let a stranger drill a hole in your head just for some quick cash. That is exactly where you start with this wild ride. You follow a homeless man who takes a weird deal from a medical student. Once the procedure is done, things get really strange. You start seeing the hidden, ugly parts of people that they try to hide from the world. The vibe is creepy and mysterious, making you feel like you are uncovering a secret world that is right in front of you but totally invisible to everyone else.

The acting is great because it makes the weird situations feel real. You will love how the movie plays with your head, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. If you enjoy stories that make you question what is real, you have to check this out. It looks amazing in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture. It is a strange trip, but it keeps you guessing until the very end.
endingExplained: You find out that the main character's new powers were mostly in his own head. The twist is that he was projecting his own loneliness and trauma onto the people he saw. In the end, he realizes that the monsters he saw in others were actually reflections of his own broken mind. He ends up losing his grip on reality completely, showing that the hole in his head broke his sanity rather than giving him a superpower.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and creepy Japanese cinema.
